'''James Lepowsky''' (born July 5, 1944) is a professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]], [[New Jersey]]. Previously he taught at [[Yale University]]. He received his Ph.D. from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1970 where his advisors were [[Bertram Kostant]] and [[Sigurdur Helgason (mathematician)|Sigurdur Helgason]]. Lepowsky graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]] in 1961,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://65.104.11.121/MathTeam.html#JLepowsky |title=Stuyvesant Math Team |accessdate=2007-10-31 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001031823/http://65.104.11.121/MathTeam.html#JLepowsky |archivedate=October 1, 2007 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> 16 years after Kostant.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www-math.mit.edu/~kostant |title=Professor Kostant's Homepage |publisher=MIT Math Department |accessdate=2007-10-31}}</ref>   His current research is in the areas of infinite-dimensional [[Lie algebras]] and [[Vertex operator algebra|vertex algebras]]. He has written several books on vertex algebras and related topics. In 1988, in a joint work with [[Igor Frenkel]] and [[Arne Meurman]], he constructed the [[monster vertex algebra]] (also known as the Moonshine module). His PhD students include Stefano Capparelli, Yi-Zhi Huang, Haisheng Li, Arne Meurman, and Antun Milas.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|5945}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>
